title: Colorado Home Battery Incentives 2026: Xcel Battery Connect
desc: Xcel Energy's Renewable Battery Connect pays Colorado homes $250 per kW up to $5,000, more for income-qualified homes, plus $100 a year for 5 years.
lead: If Xcel Energy is your power company, Colorado has one of the better home battery offers in the country. Xcel pays you upfront for the battery and a little each year, as long as it can use your battery on busy days. Here is how it works.
cards_heading: What Colorado pays for a home battery
cards_intro: Amounts come from Xcel Energy's Renewable Battery Connect page, last read on September 29, 2026.

cards.title: Renewable Battery Connect (general)
cards.note: $250 for each kW of continuous power the battery can give, up to $5,000. A battery that gives 5 kW would get $1,250.

cards.title: Income-qualified homes
cards.note: Capped at 75% of the equipment cost. Homes in a Disproportionately Impacted Community get $500 per kW, with the same 75% cap.

cards.title: Yearly payment
cards.note: Paid on top of the upfront amount while you stay enrolled.

cards.title: Federal battery tax credit
cards.note: The 30% federal credit ended for spending after December 31, 2025.

after_cards: The program reopened on May 21, 2026. Xcel's page said the general budget was $13.6 million with $11.3 million left on September 1, 2026. Money is first come, first served, so check what is left before you sign.
sections:
Xcel's offer comes with strings. The battery must be charged by solar. It must be a model Xcel accepts: on our last read, that meant a Tesla Powerwall or a current Enphase battery. And Xcel gets to use your battery during peak events, the busy summer afternoons when the grid is strained. You still get backup power in an outage.

Notice that the amount is based on kW, the power the battery can give at once, not kWh, the energy it stores. Two batteries with the same storage can earn different amounts.
If you are not on Xcel

Not every Colorado home buys power from Xcel. If your bill comes from a city-owned utility or a rural electric co-op, Xcel's program does not cover you. We have not checked those utilities' battery offers yet, so call yours and ask before you buy. Ask three questions: is there an upfront amount, is there a yearly payment, and does the utility control the battery on busy days?

Since Xcel wants the battery charged by solar, many homes add both at once. Xcel's Solar Rewards pays $1 per watt up to 10 kW in 2026, but only for income-qualified homes and homes in a Disproportionately Impacted Community. Other homes get no upfront solar payment from Xcel this year.

For a general Xcel customer, $5,000 off plus $500 over five years takes a real bite out of the price. For income-qualified homes, the per-kW amount is four times higher, so a battery can cost a fraction of the normal price. Your installer should show you the exact rebate for the battery they quote, in writing.
Questions to ask before you sign

Ask the installer to write down the battery's continuous power in kW, since that sets your rebate. Ask how many hours of backup you get for the circuits you care about. Ask what happens to your rebate if the program budget runs out before your install is done. A good installer will answer all three without fuss.
claim_heading: How to claim the Xcel battery incentive
claim_steps: Check that Xcel Energy is your electric company on your bill.
Ask your installer for a battery Xcel accepts, charged by solar.
Ask the installer to check the remaining program budget and reserve your spot.
If you think you may be income-qualified, apply for that first. The amount is much higher.
Enroll the battery so Xcel can use it during peak events, and keep it enrolled to earn $100 a year.

faq: How much does Xcel pay for a home battery in Colorado?

$250 per kW of continuous power, up to $5,000, plus $100 a year for 5 years. Income-qualified homes get $1,000 per kW and homes in Disproportionately Impacted Communities get $500 per kW, both capped at 75% of equipment cost.
Yes. Xcel's Renewable Battery Connect is for batteries charged by solar.
When we last read the page, Tesla Powerwall and current Enphase batteries. Ask your installer for the current list.
Is there a federal tax credit for batteries in 2026?
No. It ended for spending after December 31, 2025.
My bill is not from Xcel. Can I use this program?
No. Renewable Battery Connect is only for Xcel Energy customers. If a city utility or co-op sends your bill, ask it directly about battery offers.
